LESSON: CHANGE OF STATE

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
Strand: MATTER
Topic 2.1: Change of State

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Change of State
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How is change of state of matter important in day-to-day life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify the changes of state when substances are heated or cooled
2. describe the applications of the change of state of matter in everyday life
3. appreciate the applications of change of state of matter in day-to-day life

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Change of State

Teach
• Observe Change of State in real life (school compound, home, farm).
• Use safe examples only.
• Name → explain → apply.

Worked example
• Fact 1 about Change of State (in pupil words).
• Fact 2 with a Kenyan example.
• Safe action connected to Change of State.

Try this
• Draw/label one diagram for Change of State.
• Write 5 bullet facts about Change of State.
• Say one safety rule.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• identify the changes of state when substances are heated or cooled
• describe the applications of the change of state of matter in everyday life
• appreciate the applications of change of state of matter in day-to-day life

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. List 8 facts on Change of State.
2. Teach a friend using only bullet points.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet for Change of State: meaning, diagram, 5 practice questions.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How is change of state of matter important in day-to-day life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• identify the changes of state when substances are heated or cooled
• describe the applications of the change of state of matter in everyday life
• appreciate the applications of change of state of matter in day-to-day life

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
